The closest match is [1], which directly studies whether within-conversation context changes AI answers and finds that omitting preceding turns often causes materially different responses. [2] is also closely related, but it measures how request state is distributed across turns and explicitly says it does not estimate the causal effect of history on model answers.

If you mean the broader idea of context effects in multi-turn conversations, [4], [6], and [9] also address how conversational history affects model behavior, but they focus on response quality, emotion recognition, or bias rather than the specific effect on answers from omitted context.
